newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oslo bourse breaks 1,000 mark, bank cuts rates.
newsitem.headline: Oslo bourse breaks 1,000 mark, bank cuts rates.

text.p: Oslo's Total share index powered higher on Wednesday breaking the psychological 1,000-point barrier for the first time.
The index closed 1.36 percent up at 1,006.19 points, just off the intraday peak at 1,006.36 points. Turnover was a bumper 1.27 billion crowns.

Dealers said expectations of a cut in Norwegian interest rates and a firm bond market fuelled already bullish sentiment at the start of business. The Central Bank announced after the market's close it would trim its overnight deposit and lending rates by 0.5 percent to 3.5 and 5.5 percent respectively.
The cuts are effective from Thursday.

The bank has been under pressure to lower rates to dampen a strongly appreciating Norwegian crown. The crown has risen to the strongest level against European currencies since it was floated in December 1992.
Dealers said the stock-market boom was likely to continue.

"It was surprising to break through the 1,000 mark without any special news, but the economy is very good," said one broker. "The fundamental situation in Norway is very promising and therefore it's hard to get bearish."
